about.what: Raw MCP JSON-RPC 2.0 messages from one real run of the Week 9 agent: question w9-pkg-01, with config/mcp_servers.json listing docs-search and package-registry (commit ffdf62a).
about.question: Is release 2.1.0 of the example-sdk package deprecated, and if so, which release should we install instead?
about.transport: stdio: one JSON-RPC message per line, on each server subprocess's stdin (client->server) and stdout (server->client).
about.captured_by: app/mcp/client.py (WireLog, _WireTap), unchanged since Step 4: it records each message where the MCP SDK's ClientSession hands it to the stdio transport, or receives it back.
about.fidelity: 12/12 messages byte-identical to the raw pipe lines, checked with a transparent byte relay on the same system. json.dumps(message, separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=False) reproduces the exact line sent.
about.unchanged: Each 'message' value is copied unchanged from report/w9/step7_mcp_messages.jsonl. 'phase' and 'annotations' are added beside it, never inside it.
about.model_call: The model call happens in the agent, via week7_contract.chat_once as an HTTPS request to Groq's OpenAI-compatible API; it never happens on this wire, and never inside either MCP server.

tools.name: search_docs
tools.description:
Search the SDK reference documentation for prose describing what a Client method does: its behaviour, its parameter names, types and defaults, whether a parameter is required, and the caveats written in the Notes sections.

Use it when the question is about how a Client method behaves, or what one of its parameters means, defaults to, or requires.

api_version selects which version's reference pages are searched: "v2" or "v3". Only that version is searched, never both. The two versions document different defaults for the same parameter, and some methods and parameters exist only in v3. If the question names a version, pass it. If it asks to compare versions, or does not say and the answer could differ, call once per version.

query is what to look for, in words: the method and the parameter or behaviour, or just a parameter name. Leave the version out of the query; api_version already filters by it.

Returns JSON: api_version, count, and passages, best match first, each with rank, chunk_id, heading_path, score and text. Passages are ranked by similarity, not filtered for relevance, so the top one can still be off-topic: read the text before relying on it, and cite the chunk_id of any passage you use.

This tool knows nothing about HTTP paths, operation ids, or whether anything is retired, and it has no changelog or release numbers. If no passage states the answer, the documentation does not state it.

query.description: What to look for, in words or as a parameter name.

api_version.description: Which SDK version's pages to search. Required: the two versions document different defaults.

tools.name: get_package_versions
tools.description:
List every published release of one package in the package registry, with the date each release was published, and name the latest release.

Use it for questions about a package as something you install: which versions exist, which is the newest, when a release came out, or which release to pin.

package is the package's registry name, the name you would install it by, not an SDK class or method name. Case and the separators - _ . do not matter.

Returns JSON: package, found, summary, latest, and releases oldest first, each with version and released (YYYY-MM-DD). An unknown package comes back as found: false, with a reason naming the packages the registry holds.

A release number such as 1.4.2 is a package version: one published build. It is not an API or documentation version such as v3, though a package's major number may track one. This tool does not say whether a release is deprecated; get_package_deprecation answers that for one release. It says nothing about what SDK methods do, their parameters or defaults, or HTTP operations and endpoints, and it has no changelog or release notes.

package.description: Registry name of the package: the name it is installed by.

tools.name: get_package_deprecation
tools.description:
Report whether one published release of a package has been deprecated on the package registry by its maintainers, meaning that build should no longer be installed. If it has, also return the maintainers' notice, the date, and the newest release that is not deprecated.

Use it for questions like "is release 1.4.2 of this package deprecated?" or "should we still pin that release?". This is package deprecation: it is about which build of a package to install.

package is the registry name, as for get_package_versions. version is one exact release such as 1.4.2; a leading v is accepted. A release line such as 1.x or v1 is not a release: it comes back as found: false, listing the releases in that line. A release that was never published comes back as found: false, naming the latest published release. In both cases the registry answered; the release simply does not exist.

Returns JSON: package, version, found, deprecated, and when deprecated also deprecated_on, notice and replacement.

It does not answer whether an SDK method, a parameter, or an HTTP API operation or endpoint is deprecated or retired. A deprecated release says nothing about any one operation. It has no changelog or release notes.

package.description: Registry name of the package: the name it is installed by.

version.description: One exact published release, e.g. 1.4.2. Not a release line such as 1.x, and not an API version such as v3.
